version.note: The performing edition is not identified. The Internet Archive file names print the posthumous opus number 163 for the work, which Schubert’s catalogue gives as D. 956.

performers.note: The Internet Archive item lists these five performers as creators; the Substack essay assigns the roles and calls the recording a Columbia release made at the Prades Festival. Which cellist plays the first cello part and which the second is not stated in any source consulted.

date.value: 1952 (the Casals Festival at Prades); one secondary source says July
date.note: The LP sleeve notes say the recordings were made in Prades during the Casals Festival of 1952; the Discogs master release and a 6moons review also say 1952. Only the Substack essay by John Buxton gives a month, July 1952, so the month is not treated as established, and the day is not stated.

place.value: Prades, France (Prades Festival); the venue within Prades is not identified
place.note: The sleeve notes say the recordings were made in Prades during the Casals Festival of 1952. Substack says the recording was made in Prades, France during the Prades Festival; Discogs and 6moons say it was recorded at the Prades Festival in 1952.

label.note: The label is the item’s publisher metadata and the title shown on its page.

catalogue.value: ML 4714 / SL-183, Casals Festival at Prades, Third Series
catalogue.note: The Internet Archive item page prints “Columbia Masterworks (ML 4714 / SL-183)” with publication date 1953. A 1976 CBS Classics reissue (61043) and a Philips issue (A 01188 L) are listed on Discogs and are not this carrier.

matrixTakeSides.value: Side 1, second track of the LP (file 01.02 on the Internet Archive); matrix and take numbers are not established
matrixTakeSides.note: The Internet Archive file for the Adagio is a derivative linked to a segments file, so the cut between the first movement and the Adagio is the Internet Archive’s. No matrix or take numbers appear in the sources consulted.

credits.value: Internet Archive LP digitisation: ripped by an Internet Archive associate at the Cebu scanning centre (rip station archivelp-rip-cebu04); the cover was scanned and the item created by another associate
credits.note: The item metadata names a ripping operator and a ripping scanner, a scanning centre (cebu) and a separate scanning operator. The item is listed in several vinyl collections, including the Boston Public Library’s; which physical copy was digitised is not stated.

date.value: 4 January 2021 (the ripping date recorded in the item metadata)
date.note: The metadata gives ripping_date 20210104123741. The artwork scan date and public date are 24 November 2020 and the added date is 4 January 2021; these are separate events and the scan and upload dates are not transfer dates.

processing.value: Technics SL1200MK5 turntable with Audio-Technica AT95e cartridge, Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp and Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 interface; the Adagio file is an MP3 derivative of the side
processing.note: The hardware chain is the lineage field of the item metadata; the file inventory also reports generic SoX processing of the side files, with no settings. The equalisation curve, noise treatment, original recording engineering and playing-speed accuracy are not documented and are not inferred from the equipment names.

digital.format: MP3 derivative supplied by the Internet Archive

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Schubert died in 1828. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: The Internet Archive item gives publication date 1953 and the Discogs master release gives the year 1953, so the 50-year European term expired before the 2013 extension. The item carries no licence statement; no US public-domain basis is claimed, and the 1953 date is not independently verified against a label image.

alternatives.value: Pre-1963 European public domain — territorial basis, publication 1953.
No licence or rights statement on the Internet Archive item.

rights.creditLine: Franz Schubert, String Quintet in C major, D. 956, II. Adagio; Isaac Stern and Alexander Schneider, violins, Milton Katims, viola, Pablo Casals and Paul Tortelier, cellos; Prades Festival, 1952. Columbia Masterworks ML 4714 / SL-183, 1953; Internet Archive LP digitisation. Public domain in the EU only (pre-1963 publication); no worldwide recording clearance is asserted.

sources.locator: Sleeve text: “The recordings, made in Prades during the Casals Festival of 1952, are devoted to the chamber music of Schubert, Schumann and Brahms”; the Schubert Quintet in C major, Op. 163, with Stern, Schneider, Katims, Casals and Tortelier listed on the sleeve; note on the Adagio citing Einstein.

sources.title: John Buxton — Building a Collection #24: Schubert’s String Quintet in C major
sources.locator: “The Essential Recording”: recorded by Columbia Records in July 1952 in Prades, France during the Prades Festival; players Stern (then 32), Schneider, Katims, Tortelier and Casals; Casals’s grunting audible in several places; quotes Jonathan Blumhofer’s programme note.

sources.title: 6moons — Casals & friends play Schubert’s String Quintet in C Major D956
sources.locator: Review of the Sony Classical Casals Edition CD: the quintet “was recorded at the Prades festival in 1952”, with Stern, Schneider, Casals, Tortelier and Katims.
